messages:
Rahul: Quick pre-sales question for FinRegCo — they require that all PII and audit logs remain in-country (DE/IE). Can someone confirm the current EU subprocessor inventory and whether we can pin a tenant to eu-central-1 with failover only to eu-west-1? Also need a short, exact answer for the security questionnaire: 'Do any US subprocessors process customer data for an EU-only deployment?' CC @Maria

Maria: Looping in Kevin (sales-eng) and Tara (solutions). Reminder: POC starts next Wed so we need answers + wording to include in the RFP by EOD tomorrow.

Kevin: Short answers: Dedicated supports tenant-level pinning. Hosted API has region preference but not a strict hard pin. Private (on-prem/VPC) obviously fully local. I'll pull the formal subprocessor list and confirm which vendors have EU-only nodes.

Tara: For context — Hosted routing is latency-weighted and may cross borders. We do have an opt-in "geofence" routing policy for Dedicated customers that can enforce EU-only traffic. Need infra to confirm KMS/BYOK behaviour differences.

Lena: We can implement a pinning policy like:
```
routing_policy:
  mode: hard_pin
  primary: eu-central-1
  fallback: [eu-west-1]
```
But note: hard_pin requires Dedicated or Private and reserved capacity. Also callout: if strict capacity fencing is not enabled, extreme overloads could cascade fallback to non-EU regions — we can disable that.

Rahul: On the security questionnaire they asked explicitly: 'Are any US subprocessors used for EU-only deployments?' Can we answer "No" for a Dedicated EU-pinned tenant?

Kevin: If the tenant is Dedicated (or Private) and we configure strict EU-only pin + capacity fencing, then you can answer "No US subprocessors will process customer data for this tenant." For Hosted, the correct answer is "Hosted customers may be routed to non-EU subprocessors depending on capacity and routing policies." I'll provide the precise wording.

Maria: :thumbsup: Kevin — can you also include an estimated pricing uplift for reserving EU capacity (2x baseline) and any egress deltas we should tell the customer?

Kevin: Will do. Ballpark uplift is +18–25% depending on GPU class and commit length; I'll produce a short table with ranges and include egress delta to EU endpoints. Subprocessor list + pricing by EOD tomorrow.

Rahul: Last item — KMS: they want to know if they can keep key material in-country (HSM in EU). Need the exact wording to paste into the questionnaire.

Tara: BYOK details: Private: yes (customer-managed KMS/HSM in their VPC). Dedicated: yes, we support customer-managed KMS via cross-account keys in the customer's EU account. Hosted: no BYOK (Redwood-managed keys). Suggested answer: "We support customer-managed encryption keys for Dedicated and Private deployments; Hosted customers use Redwood-managed keys. Customer-managed keys are hosted in the customer's cloud account/region and do not leave that region."

Maria: Perfect. If Kevin can dump the subprocessor list + the two wording snippets (US subprocessors answer + KMS answer) into one doc, I'll attach to the RFP and share with Legal.

Kevin: On it. @OncallBot can you create a tracking ticket?

OncallBot: Created ticket PSALEADS-789: "EU data residency & subprocessor inventory for FinRegCo" — assignee Kevin — due 2026-03-25.

Rahul: Thanks everyone — I'll hold off replying to the customer until we have the doc + pricing.
